summary: I checked every information channel into every semantic role, in code and against all 20 live runs in artifacts/simulations_v3 and artifacts/matched_pairs. The resolution boundary is genuinely clean (the verbatim resolution appears in zero non-judge/non-verifier artifacts), shared_context never reaches an actor, no actor ever sees another actor's private_context, private memories, decisions or intentions, wake reasons never reach anyone, and the terminal verifier's real prompts carry only the condition, the clock and the committed record with no trace of the first judge's verdict, citations or explanation. One boundary is broken: the by_own_doing observation grant is propagated past the actor's own attempt into the downstream environmental consequence, so a sender is recorded as having OBSERVED what happened at the recipient's end -- including whether the recipient noticed. I reproduced this deterministically with the repo's own fake-transport harness and measured it in the live runs.

findings.title: A sender observes the delivery of their own message and the recipient's attention state, because by_own_doing is propagated into the environmental consequence
findings.evidence: Mechanism: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trajectory.py:227-228 sets self_act_of=actor_id for an actor_intention; trajectory.py:673-676 passes that same self_act_of into the follow-up world_step(trigger_kind="event_consequence"); trajectory.py:353-359 writes it into the scheduled K_EVENT; trajectory.py:853 and 870-874 then call journal.mark_observed(..., by_own_doing=True) on the resulting event, and journal.py:94-95 lets by_own_doing bypass the "actor_id must be in e['for']" check. Live evidence: artifacts/simulations_v3/case2_negotiation ledger.jsonl e155 "The message from Dmitri arrives on Priya's phone. She is not currently looking at her phone, so she does not notice it." for=['priya_raghavan'], observed=false, yet journal.observed seq marks actor=dmitri_sokolov source=own_doing; it is then rendered verbatim under "WHAT YOU HAVE ACTUALLY OBSERVED" in Dmitri's own prompt at actor_views.jsonl call_id c76. The mirror image reaches Priya: e49 "The message arrives in Dmitri's inbox but he has not yet seen it." and e79 "The message from Priya arrives on Dmitri's phone, but he is still occupied and does not notice it." Same defect at artifacts/matched_pairs/a1_responsive__r2 e70, artifacts/matched_pairs/b2_thornbury_lim__r3 e68, artifacts/simulations_v3/unseen2_feedback e256, artifacts/matched_pairs/c1_against_stereotype e129/e214/e242. Scale: 12 such committed events across 5 runs; 74 actor turns had one in the authoritative observed section of their prompt, including 67 of the 75 rendered views in case2_negotiation. Deterministically reproducible with no model calls by giving the repo's own test harness (tests/test_semantic_runtime.py build()/reviewed()) a world script that returns follow_up:true on an actor_intention and a delivery event on event_consequence -- the sender ends up in observed_by and the line appears in their rendered view.
findings.why_it_matters: This defeats the exact separation the runtime exists to enforce. actor_mind.py:56-58 tells the actor "you do not know what anyone else has noticed or decided" and journal.py:148-153 states the actor never sees available-unobserved items, but the sender is handed, as authoritative observed fact, both that their message physically arrived and whether the other person noticed it -- the single load-bearing uncertainty in case2_negotiation, where Priya's prompts affirmatively told her Dmitri had not seen her offer across 44 of her turns while she reasoned about whether to wait or look elsewhere. It also corrupts the judge's and verifier's evidence surface: artifacts/matched_pairs/a1_responsive__r2 review_exchanges.jsonl call c40 shows the verifier the line "e70 ... Dana Whitfield's phone or computer receives Marcus Bell's reply ... | observed by marcus_bell", i.e. an event at Dana's end that only Marcus is recorded as having seen, directly against the judge rule that anything taking two people needs BOTH to have observed it. No terminal in these 20 runs turned on that (I checked every citation: each YES rests on a genuine sending or a genuine reading), but the false observation is sitting in the record the rule is applied to.
findings.suggested_fix: Grant by_own_doing observation only for the event produced directly by that person's own actor_intention -- carry a separate flag on the scheduled event for the observation grant and do not inherit it through the event_consequence chain, leaving self_act_of to do only its "your own action gives you no fresh turn" job.

findings.title: The judge's prompts are never persisted, so the one role that receives the resolution is the one that cannot be audited from artifacts
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trace.py:86-88 writes review_exchanges.jsonl for roles ("continuity", "event_review", "verifier") only; "judge" appears in no artifact writer. Every run confirms it: artifacts/simulations_v3/case2_negotiation runtime_metrics.json reports judge_calls=40 and artifacts/matched_pairs/c1_against_stereotype reports judge_calls=33, while both directories contain zero exchanges with role "judge" (terminal_checks.jsonl carries only the parsed status/citations/explanation, never the prompt). trace.py:2-4 claims "Every prompt, raw response, parsed response, validation result, retry, simulated time, wall time, token count, causal trigger and committed record is written out."
findings.why_it_matters: The brief for this area is that the resolution must reach only the judge and the verifier, and that the judge must see committed events and nothing else. I could confirm both from trajectory.py:691-700, which passes only event_id/t/description/for/observed_by, but no artifact in any run makes that checkable after the fact -- 2 to 40 unlogged model calls per run, each carrying the one string the whole design keeps away from everyone else. Any future regression that contaminated the judge prompt would leave no trace on disk, and the docstring asserting full coverage means nobody would think to look.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "judge" to the persisted roles in trace.py:86-88 (or write judge_exchanges.jsonl alongside the others) so the resolution-bearing prompt is auditable.

findings.title: adapter.py's docstring states the opposite of the shared_context rule it is documenting
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/adapter.py:9 reads "shared_context   -> immutable background fact, given to every actor", contradicted by views.py:15-22 ("The compiled shared_context is NOT here"), by the code (journal.shared_context() is read only at trajectory.py:230 into world_mind.world_user_prompt), by tests/test_semantic_runtime.py:1789 test_the_compiled_shared_context_never_reaches_an_actor, and by all 204 rendered views on disk, none of which contain shared_context content that is not independently in that actor's own private_context or an event they observed.
findings.why_it_matters: The behaviour is correct, but this is a stale line sitting on the exact boundary under review, in the module whose job is to decide which compiled fields reach whom. It is the first thing a reader consults when deciding whether it is safe to add shared_context to a view, and it tells them it is already there.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct adapter.py:9 to say shared_context reaches the world adjudicator only, never an actor view.
